finalReport:
# OpenCut Architecture: Classic vs Rewrite — Reconciled Model

## 1. Current state in one paragraph

OpenCut is split across two lines: **Classic** is `OpenCut-app/opencut-classic`, described as the original/legacy codebase, archived May 17 2026 and read-only, while **Rewrite** is `OpenCut-app/OpenCut` main, declared to be “being rewritten from the ground up” with the previous version pointed to as “the one to reach for today” ([main README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut), [classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)). Production today is still Classic on `opencut.app`, with the rewrite preview on `new.opencut.app` until takeover ([main README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).

Classic structure is `apps/web/` Next.js web app + `apps/desktop/` GPUI native app in progress + `rust/` GPU compositor/effects/masks/WASM bindings + `docs/` ([classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic)). Rewrite intent is Editor API, plugin-first architecture, one Rust core for web/desktop/mobile, MCP server, headless mode and in-editor scripting, with engine separated from UI ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)). Rewrite today is scaffold only: `apps/web` React 19 + Vite 8 + TanStack Router/Start, `apps/api` Elysia on Workers health/echo only, `apps/desktop` Rust+GPUI early window, moon/proto orchestration ([explainer](https://mer.vin/2026/07/opencut-explained-open-source-capcut-alternative-classic-editor-vs-ground-up-rewrite/)).

## 2. Editor subsystems — what Classic actually built

### 2.1 Late-Classic: EditorCore singleton

Late-Classic docs describe a Turborepo monorepo with `apps/web/src/` containing `core/EditorCore`, `components`, `hooks`, `lib`, `services`, `stores`, `types`, `utils` plus `packages/ui` and `packages/env` ([architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

The editor is a singleton `EditorCore` coordinating 10 managers — command, playback, timeline, scenes, project, media, renderer, save, audio, selection — accessed via `useEditor()` in React and `EditorCore.getInstance()` outside React ([EditorCore concept](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/concepts/editor-core)).

Reconciled mapping for Late-Classic ([architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture), [EditorCore concept](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/concepts/editor-core)):

- `command: CommandManager` — undo/redo via Command pattern in `lib/commands/`
- `timeline: TimelineManager` — tracks, elements, split/trim/move
- `playback: PlaybackManager` — transport, seeking
- `scenes: ScenesManager` — composition/bookmarks
- `project: ProjectManager` — settings, canvas size, FPS
- `media: MediaManager` — asset loading/management
- `renderer: RendererManager` — preview + export, render tree, CanvasRenderer/SceneExporter
- `save: SaveManager` — autosave
- `audio: AudioManager` — Web Audio mixing, Mediabunny decode
- `selection: SelectionManager` — selection state
- `Actions` in `lib/actions/definitions.ts` + `use-editor-actions.ts` as UX trigger layer with toasts/validation/shortcuts; `Commands` as undoable mutation layer
- Zustand retained only for UI/app state — preferences, panels, dialogs, flags — not editor state

### 2.2 Early-Classic: Zustand full editor state

Early-Classic docs describe editor state as Zustand stores in `apps/web/src/stores/*`: `editor-store`, `timeline-store`, `media-store`, `playback-store`, `project-store`, `panel-store`, `keybindings-store`, `sounds-store`/`stickers-store` ([development docs](https://opencut.dev/docs/development/)).

Architecture diagram from the same era shows Next.js Frontend → Zustand Editor/Timeline/Media/Playback State, multi-track Timeline Canvas, Preview Panel with DOM rendering plus binary-rendering future, storage IndexedDB + OPFS, processing FFmpeg.js + bg-remover + transcription ([OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/)).

Storage is consistent across eras: IndexedDB for projects/settings, OPFS for media files, via `lib/storage/` abstraction, optional R2; workflow is import → store in OPFS → file reference → add to track → preview → FFmpeg/export → download ([OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/), [development docs](https://opencut.dev/docs/development/)).

### 2.3 Preview and export evolution inside Classic

Preview: renders with HTML/CSS/Canvas, explicitly noted as inconsistent with export, limited performance/quality; new binary rendering engine in progress for consistent preview/export; contributors told to avoid preview fonts/stickers/effects and export work during refactor ([architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

Export: evolved from placeholder export button TODO + `ffmpeg-utils.ts` to Mediabunny `Output` + `Mp4OutputFormat`/`WebMOutputFormat` + `BufferTarget` + `CanvasSource` rendering each frame via `renderTimelineFrame({tracks, mediaFiles})` reading `useTimelineStore`/`useMediaStore`/`useProjectStore`, later adding `AudioBufferSource` + `includeAudio` with opus/aac ([export commit](https://github.com/oldding/OpenCut/commit/70a9bfebb196d5c0bde35ce0a165b696bb9ae1d0)).

## 3. Are the conflicting descriptions real contradictions? No — version/time splits

The investigated contradiction — Zustand stores vs EditorCore managers — was resolved as temporal evolution, not logic conflict: early Classic used Zustand for full editor state; late Classic introduced EditorCore managers and kept Zustand only for UI. The architecture doc itself distinguishes “EditorCore managers for editor state” vs “Zustand stores for UI state” ([architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture), [EditorCore concept](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/concepts/editor-core), [development docs](https://opencut.dev/docs/development/)).

General reconciliation pattern — early-Classic vs late-Classic vs Rewrite ([OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/), [classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic), [explainer](https://mer.vin/2026/07/opencut-explained-open-source-capcut-alternative-classic-editor-vs-ground-up-rewrite/)):

| Apparent conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Next.js 15/16 App Router vs Vite 8 + TanStack Start | Next.js belongs to Classic; Vite/TanStack belongs to Rewrite scaffold |
| Zustand full editor stores vs EditorCore 10 managers | Both Classic, different times: Zustand early, EditorCore late + Zustand-UI only |
| Tauri desktop vs GPUI desktop | Tauri early Classic diagram; GPUI in-progress late Classic and Rewrite scaffold |
| Turborepo+Bun+Biome vs moon+proto | Turborepo belongs to Classic; moon/proto belongs to Rewrite |
| FFmpeg.js/`ffmpeg-utils` vs Mediabunny `CanvasSource` vs Rust GPU compositor/WASM | FFmpeg placeholder early Classic; Mediabunny canvas export late Classic; Rust compositor transitional Classic `rust/` migration and full Rewrite engine intent |
| DOM preview vs binary rendering vs stable faster renderer | DOM is Classic shipped; binary is late-Classic refactor intent that froze contributions; stable/faster renderer is Rewrite goal |
| Postgres/Drizzle/Redis/Better Auth backend vs Elysia health/echo vs Rust core | Full backend belongs to Classic web app; Elysia health/echo is Rewrite scaffold, not future Editor API; Rust core is Rewrite engine goal |

In short: if a source says Next.js + Zustand + Tauri + FFmpeg, it is describing early Classic. If it says Next.js 16 + EditorCore + GPUI + `rust/` WASM + Mediabunny, it is describing late Classic. If it says Vite + TanStack + Elysia + moon/proto + Rust core + plugins/MCP/headless, it is describing Rewrite intent/scaffold.

## 4. Reconciled model: what belongs where

### Belongs to Classic (archived, use today)

- Repo `opencut-classic`, Next.js App Router, React 18→19, TypeScript, Tailwind 4, Turborepo, Bun, Biome/Prettier, Postgres/Drizzle/Redis/Better Auth for web app concerns ([classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic), [architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture))
- EditorCore 10 managers, Actions + Commands, `useEditor()`/`getInstance()`, EventEmitter3 observer, repository pattern ([EditorCore concept](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/concepts/editor-core), [architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture))
- Early Zustand editor stores, late Zustand UI-only; IndexedDB + OPFS + storage service ([development docs](https://opencut.dev/docs/development/), [OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/))
- Timeline canvas, DOM preview, media/properties panels, WaveSurfer waveforms, FFmpeg.wasm → Mediabunny canvas export path ([architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture), [export commit](https://github.com/oldding/OpenCut/commit/70a9bfebb196d5c0bde35ce0a165b696bb9ae1d0))
- `apps/bg-remover` Python, `apps/transcription` Modal/Whisper, Tauri→GPUI desktop attempt, `rust/` GPU compositor migration via `opencut-wasm` ([development docs](https://opencut.dev/docs/development/), [classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic))

### Belongs to Rewrite (scaffold/design, preview only)

- Repo `OpenCut` main, principle “separating engine from UI”: Web/Desktop/Android/iOS → Rust core; MCP/Headless/Scripting → same core ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811), [main README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut))
- Editor API, Plugin API/host with sandboxing/lifecycle/event routing, project-storage redesign, new Web UI + built-in plugins, grouping/transitions/filters/effects expansion, captions fixes, keyboard-first opt-in ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811))
- Scaffold reality: Vite/TanStack placeholder routes, Elysia health/echo only, early GPUI window, Cargo workspace only `apps/desktop` member, `proto use` + `moon run web:dev/api:dev/desktop:dev`, contributions paused pending architecture docs, no timeline, public beta not reached ([explainer](https://mer.vin/2026/07/opencut-explained-open-source-capcut-alternative-classic-editor-vs-ground-up-rewrite/), [rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811))

### Remains uncertain / shared / transitional

- Exact Zustand→EditorCore cutover version; Mintlify docs freeze point vs `opencut-classic` HEAD ([development docs](https://opencut.dev/docs/development/), [architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture))
- Whether late-Classic binary renderer vs `rust/` GPU compositor vs Mediabunny is continuity or replacement; future renderer choice for Rewrite ([architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture), [rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811))
- Project migration mechanics `opencut.app` → `new.opencut.app` → `old.opencut.app` carry-over promise and storage-format compatibility; delivery order/timeline for Engine Core, Editor/Plugin API, Plugin host, MCP, headless, scripting, mobile ([rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811), [explainer](https://mer.vin/2026/07/opencut-explained-open-source-capcut-alternative-classic-editor-vs-ground-up-rewrite/))

## 5. How to read sources without being misled

- Check repo name first: `opencut-classic` = Classic; `OpenCut` main after May 2026 = Rewrite. Mintlify `development/architecture` and `concepts/editor-core` describe late Classic, not Rewrite ([classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic), [architecture](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- Check date/stack keywords: Turborepo/Bun/Next.js = Classic; moon/proto/Vite/TanStack/Elysia = Rewrite ([OpenCut docs](https://opencut.dev/), [explainer](https://mer.vin/2026/07/opencut-explained-open-source-capcut-alternative-classic-editor-vs-ground-up-rewrite/)).
- Treat `rust/` in Classic as transitional WASM migration, not the finished Rewrite Rust core ([classic repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic), [rewrite tracking](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).

Research completed in 2m · 49 citations · 7 searches

Scope: current OpenCut architecture and whether conflicting editor descriptions are real contradictions.

Findings: Classic is `opencut-classic` (archived) still serving production; Rewrite is `OpenCut` main scaffold. Apparent conflicts — Next.js vs Vite, Zustand vs EditorCore, Tauri vs GPUI, FFmpeg vs Mediabunny vs Rust, Turborepo vs moon/proto — are version/time splits across early-Classic vs late-Classic vs Rewrite, not logical contradictions. Late-Classic centers on EditorCore 10 managers + Actions/Commands; Rewrite centers on Rust core + Editor API/plugins/MCP/headless/scripting but is still placeholder.

Uncertain: Zustand→EditorCore cutover version, binary vs Rust renderer continuity, project migration mechanics, rewrite sequencing/timeline.
